office_does: Skagit PUD commissioners set water rates, budgets and capital projects for the county's public water utility and oversee its general manager. The whole county votes in the general election.
race_blurb: Six-year incumbent Andrew Miller, the board's president, faces real estate broker Spencer Roozen, who says rates have risen too fast and calls for line-item cost transparency. Both oppose using Skagit water for data centers. The pamphlet calls this seat Position 1; the county sample ballot labels it Position 3.

candidates.summary: Incumbent commissioner since 2020, CEO of United Way of Skagit County and Tulip Valley Farms co-founder, running on the board's record on affordability and farm water.
highlights: Says the board forged a water-sharing agreement that keeps farms irrigated in drought while protecting instream flows [S1]
Pledges to use every funding tool so modernization costs don't fall solely on ratepayers [S1]
Told the county he is 'personally opposed to the development of large-scale data centers' [S9]
Introduced a draft Water Priority Policy putting agriculture first for untreated water-rights transfers [S5]

candidates.summary: Mount Vernon real estate broker with a WSU agriculture degree, running on rate restraint, transparency and putting Skagit water users first.
highlights: Says rates rose 34% in six years; would treat rate hikes as a 'last resort' and publish line-item costs before rate votes [S3]
'Not One Drop' plank: Skagit water for Skagit users, not data centers; public hearings before major water deals [S3]
Proposes a district-wide hydrant and fire-flow review [S3]
Recommended by the Skagit County Democrats; endorsed by County Commissioners Browning and Wesen [S6][S3]
